WHERE THINGS STAND, AND WHAT IS HAPPENING

Storage is the finished picture: area is bytes, colour is category.

Scanning is the same screen while the work is going on. The map fills in cell by cell, a folder still being counted is hatched rather than coloured so an unfinished number never looks final, and the eight worker lanes show the actual parallel walk. The progress bar carries no percentage, because the scanner cannot know a total until it has walked the tree.

WHAT AN ACTION DOES, BEFORE YOU TAKE IT

The queue's footer used to be a paragraph promising the removal was safe. It is now the four steps the removal actually takes, ending at Put Back.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE LAST TIME

The same treemap, same rectangles, tinted by change instead of category: one hue each way and a neutral grey between them. Rectangles keep today's sizes, so a folder that grew is where you already know it.

The headline splits into arrived and left rather than only the net, and the panel names the seven parent folders it left out and why.

SHOWING THE WORK

Duplicates leads with the funnel: two million files in, ninety-seven out, and 0.8% of the disk actually opened to prove it. Memory stacks app memory on cache so the chart answers how full memory is, rather than drawing a flat line near the floor.
